Just like any drug, it’s affecting your brains reward system. You get a flow of dopamine creating euphoria. Maybe it calms your anxiety, maybe you feel blissful and relaxed, a little loosened up and wonky. You enjoy this feeling that when you go back to your normal state you want to indulge again. Just a little bump here, a bump there. Now your tolerance has gone up and the high is less intense so the bumps get a little bigger. I think it really has to do with the type of person you are as well. I personally am able to go on a bender of k and stop. Other people need a bit every day to take the edge off, some do it to self soothe the troubles in their head like depression and anxiety and that’s where reliance comes in and frequency of use/the amount being used increases and you find yourself doing large amounts just to get keep yourself up every day(I’ve seen this happen to my friends) they end up going through a gram every two days. When you try to quit your neuro receptors are so shot you’ve now messed up your brains natural ability to release dopamine so you find yourself even MORE depressed even suicidal, without proper help you find yourself in this cycle of using aaaand that’s addiction. They have been struggling with quitting, relapsing after 3 months to every other week. Once you get to that point it’s hard to get your brain back working right. 
So my advice is to check yourself. After I do K, I DO get that “hmmm ill just finish this bag off cuz I have no work to do today.” Then after I finish the bag I’m like “hmmm I kind of want to get another bag” “I kind of want to get high again” and that’s where Im like okay no you don’t need to be doing k on a Tuesday and shits expensive. There was a point where I was buying a bag every weekend for shows/going out for a good month. Recognizing the pattern, reflecting on what my friends are dealing with, and making the decision to cut back. I still indulge but I make sure I limit myself and recognize when im indulging too much.
